page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is a dedicated compute instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform clocked at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The server includes 192.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 5760 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent compute throughput with distinct memory strengths. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieves top 25% results with scores of 2922.47 in single-core and 69366.22 in multi-core routines. Memory subsystem bandwidth exhibits top-tier performance for uncached 256MB operations, recording 467.73 GB/sec for read and 282.99 GB/sec for write throughput. General compute and application metrics rest in the middle 50% baseline, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 10840.0, Clang compilation throughput of 23019.0, PassMark CPU score of 38720.99, and Redis SET throughput reaching 51.19 million operations per second.

The 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and 5.76 TB of fast NVMe storage offer solid qualitative resource density without the premium associated with GPU-equipped instances. However, the 2.0 GHz clock speed results in moderate single-thread execution speeds, and the architecture omits AVX-512 extensions. The server is well suited for memory-intensive databases, caching systems, analytics processing, and containerized multi-tenant workloads that require dedicated cores and large local storage capacity.
description: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an AMD EPYC instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute series, featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, 192.0 GB of RAM, and 5760 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. Its x86_64 architecture delivers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside top-tier large-block uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 467 GB/sec for reads and 282 GB/sec for writes. Synthetic stress-ng CPU tests place both single-core and multi-core output in the top 25%, while general workload metrics such as PassMark, Geekbench, and Redis throughput remain within mid-tier bounds. Balancing dense memory capacity and extensive local NVMe storage against moderate base clock speeds, the server fits large relational databases, in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and I/O-intensive enterprise applications requiring dedicated hardware allocation.
